subject: mean and cov in multiple group IRT analysis

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: mean and cov in multiple group IRT analysis
parts:
hi,

i am fitting a multiple group GRM to some data consisting of a general population sample (n = 400) and a larger patient sample (n = 4000). The mean/cov of the general population sample is fixed to 0/1, whereas the mean/cov for the patient sample is freely estimated. Item pars are constrained to be the same in both samples and freely estimated.

The fscores, however, for the general population sample are not near 0/1 as i would have expected (and it is the case if i use the patients as reference group). I suspect this is due to the large overweight of the patient data?

Best, Felix

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mean and cov in multiple group IRT analysis
parts:
Correct, I imagine you should see some pull in either direction based on the mean/cov shift. But that said anyway, secondary trait estimates don't always follow the [0,1] form, depending on the estimator (only plausible value imputations will follow the general population properties). 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mean and cov in multiple group IRT analysis
parts:
The PV distribution would resemble the implied population model in the factor scores. So if the focal group had a mean of .7 and variance of .5 (say), then most scores would not be negative in that group and the empirical summary of the groups factor scores should be close to the estimated hyper-parameters. HTH. 

Phil
